About Me
I hold a Master of Science in Digital Marketing from Cal Poly Pomona (est. graduation date: May 2026), and I bring a unique blend of skills in R programming, Python, and web analytics to every project. title: Intro to Quarto’s Capabilities for Work and School
text:
Overview
This session introduces Quarto as an open-source publishing framework that unifies code, narrative, and output to transform analyses into polished reports, presentations, dashboards, and websites. CCIDM faculty and MSDM students provide step-by-step guidance on Quarto setup in RStudio, markdown document creation with code chunks, and web publishing.




Learning Outcomes

Describe literate programming with Quarto.
Set up and use Quarto within the RStudio IDE.
List various Quarto output formats.
Render basic Quarto documents to popular document formats.
Create documents with basic markdown functions.
Explain platforms that host websites and reproducible documents.




Key Skills Gained

Literate Programming Foundations
Quarto Setup & Configuration
Markdown & Code Chunk Usage
Multi-format Rendering
Document Publishing

title: R Workshop Series #5: R Programming
text:
Overview
In this session, I introduced the principles of good coding practice in R. Participants learned about logical operators, control structures (if-statements and loops), custom function creation, and the efficient use of apply family functions. This workshop laid a solid foundation for writing clean, efficient R code.




Learning Outcomes

Practice good coding standards and techniques.

Use logical operators and control structures effectively.

Create custom R functions.

Simplify repetitive tasks using apply functions.

Familiarize with essential built-in R functions.




Key Skills Gained

Fundamental R programming

Logical and control structures

Custom function development

Code optimization

Efficient use of apply functions

title: R Workshop Series #2: R Data Types
text:
Overview
This introductory workshop covered the core data types and structures in R. Participants learned about atomic data types (numeric, character, logical) as well as more complex structures such as vectors, matrices, data frames, and lists. This session laid the groundwork for effective data manipulation in R.




Learning Outcomes

Define and differentiate between atomic data types in R.

Understand the use cases for vectors, matrices, data frames, and lists.

Learn when and how to use each data type effectively.

Create and manipulate data frames using R.

Perform basic operations to view and transform data.




Key Skills Gained

Understanding of R data types

Data structure manipulation

Creation and management of data frames

Fundamental data operations

Foundational R programming knowledge

Efficiently use built-in R datasets.

Import data from CSV, XLSX, and SPSS files.

Scrape web data using SelectorGadget and rvest.

Export and save data in different formats.

Understand the basics of version control with Git and GitHub.




Key Skills Gained

Data import/export techniques

Web data scraping

File handling in R

Version control with Git/GitHub

Practical data I/O operations

title: Featured Projects
text: Below are some key projects from my portfolio that showcase my work in digital innovation, data analytics, and interactive application development. Each project also highlights the skills I honed along the way.

title: Featured Projects
text:
Future-Proofing Airport Parking at ONT
As part of the Cal Poly Pomona CEO Business Challenge, I worked with multi-year operational data from Ontario International Airport (ONT) to explore how parking, passenger volumes, and ride-hailing activity interact over time in support of future-proof parking strategy and non-aeronautical revenue growth, while protecting all sensitive data. Using R and Quarto, I cleaned and integrated multiple datasets (parking revenue and transactions by lot, passenger counts by airline and direction, TNC trips, and lot occupancy), reshaped them into consistent monthly and weekly time series, engineered date features, standardized categories, and generated a non-sensitive schema describing table structures and missingness for safe internal sharing. I then built interactive visualizations—including stacked time-series charts, rank trajectories, inbound vs outbound flow views, TNC company-to-trip-type Sankey diagrams, and a weekly occupancy heatmap—to reveal how different parking products contribute to revenue, how usage shifts across lots, and how TNC activity compares to traditional parking, informing pricing, capacity, and product-mix decisions.
Skills Developed:

Time-Series EDA: Reshaping multi-year operational data into coherent monthly and weekly series for analysis.
Data Engineering in R: Using tidyverse, lubridate, and stringr for parsing dates, normalizing categories, and handling sparse/missing values.
Interactive Visualization: Building plotly-based stacked areas, rank plots, heatmaps, and Sankey diagrams for stakeholder-friendly exploration.
Data Governance & NDA Safety: Generating schema and missingness profiles (YAML) to document data structure without exposing raw values or sensitive metrics.

title: Featured Projects
section: A Safer Way to Collect Data: Market Area Mapping
text:
A Safer Way to Collect Data: Market Area Mapping
In my role as an Analyst, I was responsible for determining the “market area” of military installations—a process that previously involved manual note-taking at major intersections. To overcome the challenges of inaccuracy and safety risks, I developed a Shiny R application that integrates with the Strava API to automatically capture GPS data during field drives. Using the sf and leaflet packages, the app generates an interactive map of our routes, significantly enhancing both safety and data accuracy. Additionally, the HERE API is utilized to estimate market areas, adding an extra layer of verification.
Skills Developed:

Advanced R Programming: Building interactive applications with Shiny.
API Integration: Working with Strava and HERE APIs to automate data collection.
Geospatial Analysis: Using sf and leaflet for mapping and spatial data visualization.
Process Optimization: Streamlining data collection methods for improved safety and efficiency.
